To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lymphocyte preparations used for the MEM test and SCM test are not representative of the lymphocyte population of the peripheral blood from which they are derived.
(a) the MEM test is not a valid test for early cancer detection; (b) the SCM test is not a specific test for cancer detection.

(1) the MEM and SCM tests have no immunological basis and are unlikely to be clinically useful in the early detection of cancer, (2) the MEM test is a measure of non-specific morphological changes that occur in the lymphocytes during the isolation procedure, (3) the SCM test appears to be a measure of the degree of lymphocyte damage during isolation, (4) there is a need for a simple, non-invasive test that is capable of detecting the earliest stages of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an early cancer detection test using the peripheral lymphocytes of patients with clinically detected cancer and the lymphocytes of normal individuals.
the development of a test for early cancer detection based upon the interaction between isolated lymphocyte preparations and protein extracts derived from tumour cells.
the isolation of human lymphocyte preparations that are free from non-specific contamination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MEM and SCM tests are unlikely to be useful in the early diagnosis of cancer.
neither the MEM nor SCM procedures have been shown to be of any value in early cancer detection.
neither the MEM test nor the SCM test are valid general tests for early detection of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tests are not valid for the detection of early cancer.
the tests are not suitable for the detection of cancer at the earliest stages.
, at this stage, there is little evidence to indicate that these tests can be used for early cancer detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MEM and SCM tests are not suitable for use as cancer detection tests and should not be used for this purpose.
the use of peripheral lymphocytes as a general test for early cancer detection may not be valid.
it is important for any new test for early cancer detection to be validated in a large number of patients before it is used as a screening procedure.
